title: The Sertão: What Would Have Happened If...

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *si* + *hubiera* + past participle, with *habría* + past participle in the result, from B1 Unit 35: it talks about a past that did not happen. In the sertão, a dry region of the Northeast, it is natural to ask what would have changed with more rain or a different history. Here the pattern works on the sertão, the cangaço and cordel.

sections.title: If it had..., it would have...
rows: Si hubiera llovido más, muchas familias no habrían salido del sertão.
*si hubiera llovido* + *habrían salido*: if it had rained more, they would not have left
Si los campesinos hubieran tenido tierra, habrían vivido mejor.
*hubieran tenido* ... *habrían vivido*: if they had had land
Si no hubiera existido el cordel, muchas historias no habrían llegado a las ferias.
Si hubiera podido, el poeta habría impreso más folletos.
the same pattern in the singular

items.spanish: Si hubiéramos visitado el sertão en junio, habríamos oído forró.
items.english: If we had visited the sertão in June, we would have heard forró.

items.spanish: Si la sequía hubiera terminado antes, la gente no habría emigrado.
items.english: If the drought had ended earlier, people would not have emigrated.

items.spanish: Si hubieras comprado un folleto, habrías leído esa historia.
items.english: If you had bought a leaflet, you would have read that story.

sections.content: Both parts use *haber*: *hubiera* in the *si* clause, *habría* in the result. Never *si habría*. The pattern is for a past that did not happen, so these sentences are guesses about what could have been, not facts.
